title: Oracle Moves Gas by Trucks to Avoid Data Center Power Delays
key_facts: Oracle is trucking compressed natural gas to AI data centers that cannot yet connect to a pipeline.
Road deliveries kept a site outside Salt Lake City moving for more than a year and are powering early work at an OpenAI campus in Shackelford County, Texas.
Certarus supplied the Utah deliveries and VoltaGrid the Texas ones.
Delivered gas costs about four times a major hub price once labour, equipment and fuel are counted, East Daley Analytics told Bloomberg.
Oracle is weighing the same approach at Project Jupiter in New Mexico, where the State Land Office twice refused rights-of-way for Energy Transfer's pipeline and the start date slipped to February.
Oracle did not reply to Bloomberg's request for comment; its shares fell about 5.5%.
Oracle's free cash flow is negative and expected to stay so until the sites are finished.
quote_evidence: Oracle is trucking compressed natural gas to data centres it cannot plug in.
Delivered, it runs about four times the price of gas at a major hub once labour, equipment and the trucks’ own fuel are counted, East Daley Analytics told Bloomberg.
Oracle’s free cash flow is negative and expected to stay that way until the sites are finished.
why_it_matters_hint: Grid and pipeline delays are pushing AI builders to expensive trucked fuel.
notes: Bloomberg original not readable here (robot check); text from The Next Web, which credits Bloomberg. Cost figures are analyst estimates.
